basis: Operator decision 2026-10-12, option A: treat US federal government works as public domain for this source, record the reasoning, and proceed to construction rather than seek explicit written permission first. MSHA publishes no licence, no terms of use and no redistribution permission on the data-set landing page or in the Violations definition file; the data.gov catalogue entry carries accessLevel: public with rights: "true" and names no licence. The only basis for redistribution is therefore statutory - works of the US federal government are not subject to copyright (17 USC 105) - which is an argument, not a document the publisher can be quoted on. Two independent third parties already redistribute derived MSHA data under open dedications (emperor-mew/msha-violations, CC0; FastDOLz/msha-mine-safety-violations-by-operator, CC-BY-4.0, Zenodo DOI 10.5281/zenodo.20572372); the operator weighed that as precedent, and it is not treated here as a permission from the publisher. No publisher grant is claimed anywhere in this release. This decision is specific to this source id and could not be inherited silently from another candidate. If MSHA publishes terms, or the operator narrows this decision, this file is where the change lands, and release-manifest.py will carry the change into the manifest automatically.

compilation.scope: Our contribution: the row selection, the derived multi-label target (the set of 30 CFR sections cited at one inspection), the declared prediction instant, the temporal partitions, the feature construction and the packaging. The dedication covers our contribution only. It does not cover or relicense the source rows: those are published by MSHA without terms and are redistributed here as US federal government works.

source.status: Public Domain by statute (US federal government work), preserved unchanged. The publisher states no terms, no licence and no redistribution permission; the public-domain character rests on 17 USC 105, not on a quotable grant.
evidence: [MSHA Violations Data Set landing page and the publisher's own definition file, read 2026-09-27] https://www.msha.gov/data-and-reports/data-sources-and-calculators/data-resources/mdsrg/violations-data-set and https://arlweb.msha.gov/OpenGovernmentData/DataSets/Violations_Definition_File.txt publish the files, the 50 column definitions and the weekly update frequency; they state no licence, no terms of use and no redistribution permission.

[data.gov catalogue entry for the MSHA Violations Dataset, read 2026-09-27] https://catalog.data.gov/dataset/msha-violations-dataset carries accessLevel: public, rights: "true", publisher: Mine Safety and Health Administration, temporal 2000-01-01 to present. It names no licence; public-domain status is by statute, not by that entry.

[Third-party precedent, read 2026-09-27, precedent only - not a grant] https://huggingface.co/api/datasets/emperor-mew/msha-violations declares license: cc0-1.0 for its derived MSHA data and states the underlying federal works are US public domain (citing 17 USC 105); https://huggingface.co/api/datasets/FastDOLz/msha-mine-safety-violations-by-operator publishes a CC-BY-4.0 mirror of the same source, registered on Zenodo (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.20572372).

[Operator decision, 2026-10-12] The operator selected option A after the two options were put to them explicitly: (a) treat US federal works as public domain, record the reasoning and the data.gov accessLevel=public entry, and proceed; or (b) require explicit written permission before any construction. Option A was chosen. This is a recorded decision with its reasoning, not an assumption made in the pipeline.
